correctness.rationale: The exact tangent-line intersection and Green area formula reproduce Michalska 2003 Eq. (1.1), then Fourier orthogonality yields recurrence c_k=(k-2)q_{k-1}/2-(k+2)q_{k+1}/2. Weighted odd/even telescoping reconstructs all powers; C2 Parseval controls tails, and c1 plus the even recurrence recovers R>0. The analytic two-oval counterexample has radius of curvature at least 9 and nonmatching second/third-harmonic phases. Standalone numerical Green integration and exact synthetic recurrence checks passed; neither is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural inverse-geometry problem is completely classified: infinitely many Fourier magnitudes, perimeter and enclosed area are recoverable from a scalar visual-angle area observable, while phases form exactly the ambiguity. The explicit parity telescoping, infinite-tail control and noncongruent analytic witnesses give a motivated structural answer, beyond computing one forward area.
